title: ships.toml: FleetLedger's inventory (~/.config/fleetledger/ships.toml)
description: Local and git-ignored: it holds your accounts, names and paths. Read and written by FleetLedger only (W3, W8, W9, W10). The repo ships contracts/examples/ships.toml/ with generic values. See contracts/settings.md.

admin_key.description: Private key FleetLedger uses to log in as the fleet user. Its .pub goes into every seed.

agent_keys.description: Public key files placed in the agent user's authorized_keys (your keys for attaching).

known_hosts.description: FleetLedger's own known-hosts file; never your ~/.ssh/known_hosts.

managed_keys.description: Private keys FleetLedger made (or took over) and protects itself: each is encrypted with a random passphrase that FleetLedger keeps and types for you (into ssh-keygen and ssh-add, never on a command line), loading the key into ssh-agent when it is needed. Keys not listed keep the passphrase you chose.

store.description: Where the passphrases are kept. keyring: the OS keyring, service "fleetledger", item key-passphrase:<key file name>. file: ~/.config/fleetledger/key-passphrases/<key file name>, mode 0600.

keys.description: The private key files (admin key, CA keys, your own key if FleetLedger made it).

defaults.description: Applied to new Ships unless the ship-fleet new command overrides them.

image.description: The pinned base image for new Ships: an id from [image], or "stock" (the driver's own template, made from Ubuntu's cloud image). Absent: stock. Set with `ship-fleet image use`.
Baked base images (contracts/image.md), keyed by image id. Written by `ship-fleet image build` and `image publish`.

tag.description: Expected accounts per tag. After every sign-in, and on every status poll, the signed-in account is compared with these.

profile_options.description: Default option values per profile (e.g. a repo URL), copied into each Ship's ship.toml.

ca.description: FleetLedger as the fleet's SSH certificate authority (phase 3). Absent until `ship-fleet ca init`.

host_key.description: Private key that signs Ships' host certificates (its .pub sits beside it). Keep it passphrase-protected; FleetLedger signs through ssh-agent when the key is loaded there.

user_key.description: Private key that signs trusted machines' user certificates (its .pub sits beside it). A separate key from host_key.

host_cert_days.description: Validity of new host certificates. `ship-fleet ca sign` renews those within 30 days of expiry.

user_cert_hours.description: Default validity of trusted machines' user certificates.

previous_user_keys.description: Old user CA public keys Ships still accept while a CA rotation is in progress.

revoked_host_keys.description: Host keys that must never be trusted again (Ships re-keyed or removed after being certified). Trusted machines refuse them (RevokedHostKeys).

machine.description: Machines you attach from (herdr --remote, plain SSH), keyed by a name you choose. Each gets short-lived user certificates for the agent user (`ship-fleet trust`).

public_key.description: The machine's own public key. Its private half never leaves that machine.

scope.description: Which Ships the certificates open: all, tag:<tag>, or ship:<name>. Becomes the certificate principals agent:all, agent:tag:<tag>, agent:ship:<name>.

cert_hours.description: This machine's certificate validity, overriding ca.user_cert_hours.

issued.description: Certificates issued to this machine that may not have lapsed yet, kept so a narrower scope can revoke the wider ones. Any whose principals the current scope no longer covers are revoked by serial in the list every Ship gets. Written by ship-fleet; lapsed entries are dropped.

ca.description: Fingerprint of the user CA key that signed it.

revoked.description: When `ship-fleet untrust` revoked it. Its key is in the revocation list every Ship gets, and it is never certified again.

ship.description: One entry per Ship, keyed by Ship name.

imageId.description: e.g. 26.04-20261102-3f9a1c2e: Ubuntu release, bake date, first 8 hex of the bake inputs' hash.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the baked qcow2 file; checked before every publish.

file.description: The local qcow2, if it is still kept.

recipes.description: Catalogue recipes marked bake whose system parts are in the image.

published.description: Where the image is ready to clone from, per driver, e.g. { proxmox = { template_vmid = 9181 } }.

overlay.description: The overlay network Ships join for access off the LAN (phase 5, docs/runbooks/remote-access.md). FleetLedger hands each Ship a one-off key over SSH after boot; keys never go into seeds.

provider.description: tailscale: Tailscale's hosted service (login_server optional, for compatibility). headscale: your own Headscale server at login_server; keys are pasted (key_source prompt). See docs/overlay-providers.md.

login_server.description: Coordination server for Headscale. Absent: Tailscale's own.

tags.description: Overlay tags every Ship joins with. The key must allow them.

key_source.description: prompt: you paste a one-off key, read without echo. tailscale-api: FleetLedger mints a single-use, pre-approved, tagged key with an OAuth client (api).

secret_store.description: Where the OAuth client secret is kept. keyring: the OS keyring (Secret Service on Linux, Keychain on macOS), item keyring_item under the service "fleetledger"; protects it at rest, but an unlocked keyring is readable by any process of the same user. file: oauth_secret_file, mode 0600. ships.toml never holds the secret itself.

oauth_secret_file.description: File holding only the OAuth client secret, mode 0600 (secret_store = file).

remove_devices.description: Opt-in: destroy removes the Ship's device through the API. It needs the devices:core scope, which Tailscale grants over the whole tailnet: a leaked secret could then remove any device. Off (the default): the secret only mints keys, and destroy prints the admin-console step to remove the device.

manage_policy.description: Opt-in: the OAuth client also has the policy_file scope, and `ship-fleet overlay setup` may merge the Ships' rules into the tailnet policy (after showing a diff and asking). The stored secret can then change access rules. Off: FleetLedger only reads and checks the policy.

permissionMode.description: Claude Code permission modes; "default" is the mode Claude Code calls Manual.

remote_control.description: on: remoteControlAtStartup true. off: remoteControlAtStartup false and disableRemoteControl true, which also keeps resumed sessions from reconnecting. blocked: an older name for off, identical to it; still accepted.

allow_bypass.description: false writes permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode = "disable" to managed settings.

session_prefix.description: Session names: sessions the Ship starts are named <session_prefix>-<agent> (claude --name). Also set as the Remote Control name prefix, which only names a session before its first message. Default: the Ship's name.

timestamp.description: UTC, RFC 3339, with a Z suffix.

path.description: A local file path; ~/ is expanded.

seed_storage.description: ISO-capable storage used only for seed ISOs.

disk_storage.description: Storage for the Ships' VM disks (the full clone's target). Required, with no default: storage names differ from server to server.

image_storage.description: Storage with the import content type, used only to upload baked images (`ship-fleet image publish`). Optional: without it images cannot be published through the API.

token_store.description: Where the token secret is kept. keyring: the OS keyring (Secret Service on Linux, Keychain on macOS), item keyring_item under the service "fleetledger"; protects it at rest, but an unlocked keyring is readable by any process of the same user. file: token_file, mode 0600. ships.toml never holds the secret itself.

keyring_item.description: The keyring item's name (token_store = keyring); `ship-fleet setup` uses proxmox-token:<token_id>.

token_file.description: File holding only the token secret, mode 0600 (token_store = file).

tls_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the API's TLS certificate, colon-separated upper-case hex.

vmid_range.description: Optional [first, last] VMIDs FleetLedger may allocate.

driver_ref.description: Driver-specific handle, e.g. { vmid = 101 } for proxmox.

names.description: Hostnames to try in order (LAN name first, overlay name later). Never bare IPs in shared examples.

host_key.description: The Ship's ed25519 host public key, pinned before first boot.

enrolled.description: When FleetLedger finished enrolment (contracts/seed.md): provisioning done, seed detached and deleted. Absent until then.

image.description: The base image the Ship was created from. Absent on Ships made before images existed (stock).

overlay_node.description: The overlay node id the Ship joined as (`ship-ctl overlay join`), recorded so its device can be removed by identity, never by name alone.
